subject: Computer Networking
title: GraphQL: Query What You Need
description: A quick, practical guide to GraphQL: Query What You Need.

hook.text: A REST API returns 50 fields. You only need 3. GraphQL lets you ask for exactly what you want.

buildup.text: GraphQL defines a schema. Clients write queries specifying the exact shape of data they need returned.

discovery.text: One endpoint serves all queries. No more juggling dozens of REST URLs for different data combinations.

twist.text: GraphQL shifts complexity to the server. Poorly written queries can accidentally request massive data joins.

climax.text: Facebook created GraphQL in 2012. GitHub, Shopify, and Yelp all offer public GraphQL APIs today.

punchline.text: GraphQL asks only for what it needs. No more, no less.

quiz.question: What advantage does GraphQL have over REST?
options: Clients request only the exact data fields they need
It uses binary encoding for faster transfers
It works without an internet connection

details.summary: GraphQL is an API query language that lets clients request exactly the data they need in a single request, unlike REST where each endpoint returns a fixed structure. Clients define the shape of the response, eliminating over-fetching and under-fetching problems common in REST APIs.
details.whyItMatters: GraphQL solves real performance problems for frontend applications that need data from multiple resources. It reduces network requests and bandwidth by letting clients specify precisely what they need.
takeaways: Clients define the exact shape and fields of each response
A single request can fetch data from multiple related resources
Eliminates the over-fetching and under-fetching of REST APIs

faq.question: How does GraphQL differ from REST?
faq.answer: REST exposes fixed endpoints that return predetermined data structures. GraphQL exposes a single endpoint where clients specify what data they want. REST often requires multiple requests to assemble related data, while GraphQL fetches everything in one query with exactly the requested fields.

faq.question: What are the downsides of GraphQL?
faq.answer: GraphQL adds complexity to the server with schema definition and resolver implementation. Caching is harder than REST because queries are dynamic. Deeply nested queries can cause performance problems without rate limiting. Some teams find REST's simplicity more appropriate for straightforward APIs.
